title: Osho on Love Without Holding
description: What Osho taught about love and freedom, in plain words. Why does love so often turn into a cage? A rich man and the bird he kept in gold, the Sufi lover who knocked at the door and was not let in, the drop that is afraid of the ocean, and the difference between picking a flower and watering it. Then a meditation for the heart.

chapters.title: Osho on Love Without Holding
chapters.ref: Osho, Autobiography of a Spiritually Incorrect Mystic

beats.say: Everybody wants love. Have you seen any man, any woman, who does not want love? And yet, look around you. How many people are really happy in their love?
Love begins like a song. Two people meet, and the whole world becomes new. And then, slowly, slowly... the song becomes a quarrel, and the quarrel becomes a cage.
Osho said: "Love gives you the roots into the earth, and freedom gives you the wings." Tonight, let us talk about a love that does not hold. A love that has open hands.
It is rare. But it is possible. And Osho taught that it begins not with another person... it begins with you.

chapters.title: The Bird in the Golden Cage

beats.say: There was a rich man who loved birds. One day he found the most beautiful bird in the whole country, with feathers of every colour and a voice like water.
He wanted to keep it forever. So he made a cage of pure gold, and he put the bird inside, and every day he gave it the finest seeds and the cleanest water.
But the bird stopped singing. Day after day it sat in the corner of the golden cage, silent. The man could not understand. I have given it everything.
A Sufi wanderer was passing by. He looked at the cage, and at the man, and he asked: Tell me, do you love the bird... or do you love the cage?
The man was silent for a long time. Then, with trembling hands, he opened the door of the cage. And the bird flew away into the sky.
He cried that night. But the next morning, when he woke up, he heard singing at his window. The bird had come back. Free... and singing.
For Osho, love and freedom go together. What is held, dies. What is free, returns, if it wants to. And if it does not return... it was never yours.
Ordinarily, what we call love is need. I am empty, you are empty. I want you to fill me, you want me to fill you. Two beggars, each begging from the other.
And beggars cannot give. How can a beggar give? So soon there is complaining. You don't love me enough. You have changed. You don't understand me.
There is another kind of love. It comes when you are already full. When you are happy alone, sitting under a tree, wanting nothing.
Then love is not a need. It is an overflowing. Like a cloud full of rain, it has to give. It gives because it is full, not because it wants something back.
Such a person does not cling. He does not say: you must be mine. He says: be yourself, and let me share my joy with you, as long as we both like it.
Osho taught: first learn to be alone, happily alone. Only one who can be alone is capable of love.
The great Sufi poet Rumi tells a story. A lover came and knocked at the door of the one he loved. And from inside a voice asked: Who is there?
It is I, said the lover. And the voice said: There is no room here for you and me. Go away. And the door stayed closed.
The lover went away into the desert. For a whole year he wandered, alone, burning, thinking about that closed door.
Then he came back and knocked again. And again the voice asked: Who is there? And this time the lover said: It is you.
And the door opened.
Osho taught: as long as there is an I, love is a bargain. When the I disappears, love becomes a prayer. The door was never locked. Only you were standing in the way.
Jealousy is the shadow of a love that is afraid. You are afraid that the one you love will be taken away. So you watch, you suspect, you hold tighter.
But try to hold water in your fist. The tighter you hold, the faster it runs out between your fingers.
Open your hand, and the water rests in your palm. It is the same with love. Open hands can hold everything. A fist holds nothing.
When jealousy comes, don't fight it, don't act on it. Watch it. See the fear underneath it. And the fear will tell you: I am not yet full enough to love.
Osho taught: watch the jealousy, don't fight it. That is not bad news. That is the beginning of real love.

chapters.title: The Drop and the Ocean
chapters.ref: A Sufi image · Osho, Come, Come, Yet Again Come

beats.say: A drop of water is falling from a cloud towards the ocean. And the drop is afraid. If I fall into the ocean, I will be lost. I will die.
The drop is right, in a way. It will be lost as a small drop. Its little shape, its little boundary... gone.
But the Sufis say: the drop does not die in the ocean. It becomes the ocean. It loses its smallness, and it gains the whole.
This is love. To be lost in something bigger than yourself. That is why love frightens us... and that is why nothing else can satisfy us.
Osho said: "My whole teaching consists of two words, meditation and love." Every love story is a small rehearsal for that great falling.

chapters.title: Picking the Flower, Watering the Flower

beats.say: A man walks in a garden and sees a beautiful rose. He says: I love this flower. And he picks it, and takes it home, and puts it in a glass of water.
In two days the flower is dead. He loved it, and his love killed it.
Another man sees the same rose. He also says: I love this flower. And he waters it, and protects it from the goats, and comes every morning just to look at it.
The first man's love is possession. The second man's love is care. One takes. The other gives... and the rose goes on blooming.
Osho taught: love that possesses is not love. Look at your own love. Are you picking the flower? Or are you watering it?
We think love is a relationship. Something between two people, like a bridge. And so we are always worried about the bridge. Is it strong enough? Will it break?
But real love is not a relationship. It is a state of being. It is not something you do. It is something you are.
Look at a flower in the forest. Its fragrance goes on spreading, whether anyone passes by or not. It does not wait for a customer.
A man of love is like that. He is loving when he speaks to his wife, and loving when he speaks to the postman. Loving even when he is alone in his room.
His love does not depend on you. So he cannot be hurt so easily. And he does not need to hold you, because he is not afraid of losing his love.
You can leave, and the love remains. You can come back, and the love is there to welcome you. Like the sky. It never closes the door.
Osho said: "Nobody can teach you love. Love you have to find yourself, within your being." So don't ask: who will love me? Ask: how can I become loving?
Now sit comfortably, and close your eyes. This is a heart meditation in the spirit of Osho's teaching. Put both your hands on your heart. Feel the warmth of your own hands.
Feel the heart beating underneath. It has been beating for you all your life, day and night, without asking anything.
Breathe into the heart. As if the breath is going in and out, through the chest. Slowly... softly.
Now remember someone you love. Not to hold them. Just to feel the love, like a warm light in the chest.
Let that light grow. Let it go beyond that one person. To your family, your neighbours, the people in the street. To the trees, the birds, the stars.
You are not giving anything away. The more you give, the more there is. Love is the only thing that grows when it is shared.
Now rest. Don't send the love anywhere. Just be it. A lamp does not choose who will receive its light.
And slowly, take a deep breath. Open your eyes. Go into your day with open hands, my friend.
